verdict: Udaipur hospitality is lendable on a selective basis — back licensed, cash-generating hotels and restaurants riding the Diwali demand surge, and decline unapproved rooftop conversions and GST-stressed budget operators.
title: Udaipur Tourism, Hotels & Restaurants: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A Udaipur hotel or restaurant sells a perishable room-night or a table, and cash arrives the same day it is sold.** Inputs are staff, power, food and beverage, and rent or EMI on the property; the working-capital cycle is short and mostly cash, so the real risk sits in capex and in the licence, not in receivables. **Pricing power is seasonal and event-led** — the local report shows 60% of hotel rooms booked for Diwali with tariffs reaching Rs 1.5 lakh [1]. That is a peak, not a base; underwrite the annual average, not the festival week.

## What has changed now
**Demand is visibly hot in the city this season** — the Diwali booking surge and the Rs 1.5 lakh peak tariff are the freshest local signal [1]. **The trade is lobbying on tax, which tells you margins are being squeezed at the policy level**: Hotel Association Udaipur has written to the Union Finance Minister seeking 7 GST reforms, including an ITC demand and a Rs 7,500–10,000 tariff slab [3]. **Separately, the Old City has an unsafe rooftop build-out** — illegal rooftop restaurants raised with iron and wood, flagged as a fire-safety risk [2]. So when a proposal lands, check the fire NOC and municipal approval first; if the rooftop is unapproved, ask for the sanctioned plan and decline if it is absent.

## Where the growth is
**Peer results confirm the upcycle is real, not local hype.** ITC Hotels Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% with EBITDA up 37% [4]; Leela's Q2 was driven by 30% RevPAR growth, entirely ARR-led, on domestic travel and MICE demand [6]; Ventive posted 27% revenue growth at a 48% EBITDA margin [5]. **Pursue licensed boutique and heritage hotels with steady occupancy, MICE-capable banquet properties, and established F&B operators with owned or leased premises.** Avoid unapproved rooftop conversions [2] and thin-margin budget lodges leaning on GST relief [3]. Note the sources say little about Udaipur-specific financials — lean on first principles and these peers.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the season, not the peak.** Size the loan on the lean-month cash flow, take monthly stock and sales statements plus GST returns, and covenant a minimum occupancy or covers-per-day floor. **Take the fire NOC, licence and lease deed on file at sanction** [2], and require quarterly rent or EMI proof. Where a borrower claims festival-level tariffs [1], ask for the trailing twelve-month average room rate — collect from customer.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch for tariff claims that only cite the Diwali peak [1], licence or NOC lapses [2], and any GST-slab dispute hitting billing [3].** A drop in monthly GST turnover or occupancy below the covenant floor means stop fresh disbursal and re-price.
